questions.question: What is the state of matter formed by cooling a gas of extremely low density to Super low temperatures?
questions.solution:
• Conventionally we are aware of three states of matter Solid, Liquid and Gas. But over the years scientists have been discussing two additional states of matter i.e. Plasma state and Bose-Einstein Condensate.
 
• Plasma is the state in which particles are in the Super energized and super excited state.
 
• **Bose-Einstein condensate is formed when particles at low densities are cooled to super-low temperature like absolute zero (-273.5 degrees Celsius). **
 
• This concept was first put by S N Bose and later developed by Albert Einstein and thus came to be known as Bose-Einstein condensate.
 
• In 2001 Eric Cornell, Carl E. Weiman, and Wolfgang were awarded the Nobel for achieving this state.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of momentum?
questions.solution:
SI Unit of Momentum = **Kg m/s.**

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__**Momentum:**__

__
 
• Momentum is the product of the mass of an object and the velocity it is moving with.
 
• Hence SI unit of momentum is the product of SI units of mass and Velocity.
 
• SI Unit of Mass= Kg.
 
• SI Unit of Velocity = Meter per Second (m/s).
 
 
• **So, SI Unit of Momentum = Kg m/s.**
 
 
 
• The dimensional formula for momentum is MLT⁻¹.

questions.question: Tripitaka is the holy book of which of the following religions?
questions.solution:
• **"Tripitaka" are the three holy books of Buddhism. They were compiled at Buddhist Council. The Tripitaka includes:**

 
 
• Vinaya Pitaka: It contains the codes to be followed by the Monks. It was composed by Mahakasapa (a Buddhist monk).
 
• Sutta Pitaka: It was composed by Ananda at the first Buddhist council, and contains the teaching of Buddha.
 
• Abhidhamma Pitaka: It was composed at the third council which was held under Ashoka at Patliputra.

questions.question: Which human organ is responsible for removing nitrogenous waste from the human body?
questions.solution:
__
 
• Human Excretory system is responsible for removing waste and to maintain salt-water balance in the body.
 
• During the normal metabolism of the body especially breaking down of protein nitrogenous waste is produced such as urea.
 
• Here **kidney __plays an important role in the purification of blood by removing the wastes. It removes the urea which is excreted out and blood goes back to the heart again. **
 
• Excess water is flushed out in the form of urine but the kidney helps the body to retain the necessary amount of water.
 
• When normal kidney functioning is abrupt then the patient has to go through an external dialysis process to maintain blood purification and flush out toxic wastes.
 
• Lungs are the primary organ helping in the respiration process while the pancreas secretes insulin which helps to control body sugar 

 
 

 
 
**Body organ **

 
 
 
**Nature **

 
 
 
**Essential function **

 
 
 
**Importance**

 
 
 

 
 
**Lungs**

 
 
 
lungs are sponge-like organs.

 
 
 
 Every time person breathe lungs filter oxygen from the air.

 
 
 
lungs filter carbon dioxide from your body when you breathe out.

 
 
 

 
 
**Kidney**

 
 
 
kidneys are also filters.

 
 
 
Drugs are filtered more by the kidneys than by the liver.

 
 
 
Waste products filtered by the kidneys leaves the body as urine.

 
 
 

 
 
**Liver **

 
 
 
Liver is the organ below the lungs.

 
 
 
Lungs acts like a filter for the blood.

 
 
 
The liver is the only internal organ that can regrow

 
 
 

 
 
**Pancreas**

 
 
 
Pancreas is a pistol shaped gland below the liver.

 
 
 
It releases digestive enzymes into the small intestine and hormones that control sugar levels in your blood.

 
 
 
You can live without a pancreas but you need to take insulin to regulate blood sugar levels

questions.question: The decisions of the Supreme Court of India are binding on _________.

options.text: All States & UT except J & K

questions.solution:
__
 
• In India, the Supreme court is at the helm of judicial structure in India.
 
• The Supreme Court and High Courts are also called the court of record. It means that they the power to punish anyone for contempt of its orders.
 
• **Again, Article 141 of the constitution of India provides that the orders of the Supreme Court shall be binding on the other courts within the territory of India.**
 
• It is pertinent to note here that although the Supreme Court's decision is binding on all courts of India, it is **not binding on Supreme Court itself**__ which means that __**Supreme Court do has the power to override it's earlier decisions**__.
 
• However, the general superintendence of the district and other subordinate courts in any state is vested in their respective high courts.
 
• But the orders passed by the Supreme Court can supersede that of any High Court. Supreme Court is also a __**highest court of appeal**__ in India.

questions.question: Right to Health is guaranteed to every citizen of India under which article?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Article 21**__ is one of the most expanded articles of the constitution of India and over the years it has brought out various derived rights under it.
 
• Article 21 provides the Right to Life and Personal Liberty and also includes:
 
 
• **Right to privacy.**
 
• Right to a good environment.
 
• Right to travel abroad.
 
• Right to sanitation.
 
• Right to a fair and speedy trial.
 
• Right to have a dignified life.
 
• **Right to health: State of Punjab V. Mohindar Singh Chawala, the apex court ruled that right to health is included under the ambit of right to life. This article also provides the right of patients to be treated with dignity, the right to medical confidentiality.**

questions.question: Which is the highest Court of Appeal in India?
questions.solution:
__
 
• In India there is a system of the single-integrated judiciary, meaning there is only one court for both laws enacted by Union (Parliament) and States (their Legislative Assemblies).
 
• However, there is a hierarchical structure of courts with the supreme court at the helm followed by high courts and then the subordinate courts.
 
• Article 124 of the Constitution of India mandates having a **Supreme court**__.

• Supreme court in its capacity acts as the prime resolver of Federal disputes between central or state or between two or more states.
 
• It is the guardian of Fundamental Rights and interpreter of the constitution.

questions.question: Pricing Policy of Minimum Support Price follows which approach?
questions.solution:
__
 
• Minimum Support Price (MSP) is a form of market intervention by the government of India to protect farmers from the sharp fall in agricultural farm prices.
 
• MSP is announced on the recommendation of the Commission for Agricultural Cost and Prices (CACP) and approved by Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs.
 
• It is announced usually before the sowing season of crops. Presently, there are 24 crops covered under this MSP scheme.
 
• **The determining mechanism of MSP is the Cost Plus approach__ considered by CACP which includes: cost of factors of production, changes in input prices, trends in market prices, demand-supply, etc. **
 
• National Commission for Farmers has recommended that MSP should be 50% higher than the cost.

questions.question: Which of the following pillars depict rock-cut pillars?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Maurya Pillar**__ Architecture was comprised of four parts: 

 
 
• Shaft: a long shaft from the ground which provided a base and was usually made of a single stone or cut out of a single monolith.
 
• Capital: upon that shaft was capital usually lotus or something bell-shaped.
 
• Abacus: provided resting platform for the figure which was put on top.
 
• Capital Figure: usually a Lion, Elephant, or bull either standing or sitting was carved on the top.
 
 
 
• Both Mauryan and Achemeninan (Persian) pillars used polished stones.
 
• **Mauryan Pillars** were rock-cut out of single monoliths.
 
• **Gothic pillar **comes within Gothic Architecture which is also called Pointed Architecture.
 
 
• Three essential elements of Gothic Architecture are:
 
 
• I) The pointed arch
 
• II) The rib vault
 
• III) The flying buttress
 
 
 
 
 
• **Achaemenid Architecture **(**Persian**) is an extraordinary architectural legacy starting from Cyrus the Great's solemn tomb in Pasargadae to the extraordinary structures of the Persepolis.
